title: Builder Signals · 2026-07-24
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 35 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 11 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
featured.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie shared and endorsed a piece from Anthropic's Head of Economics with a counterintuitive core finding: jobs have been less negatively impacted by AI than expected. The reason is that AI still requires people to operate to produce value—most jobs can't be fully automated, only certain tasks within them. And when you automate specific tasks, you actually get more output from those jobs, raising or maintaining demand. He quotes: "So far, AI is both skill-biased and labor-augmenting. It complements d…
featured.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 转发并点评了 Anthropic 经济研究负责人的一篇文章，核心观点很反直觉：AI 对就业的负面冲击远小于预期。原因是到目前为止 AI 仍然需要人来操作才能产生价值——大多数工作无法被完全自动化，只有其中某些任务能被自动化。而当你自动化掉特定任务后，反而能从这份工作里榨出更多产出，从而抬高（或至少维持）对它的需求。他引用原文说「AI 既是技能偏向型的，也是劳动增强型的。它补足领域专长，依赖人在回路中去指挥和评估最复杂的工作。」软件工程就是最明显的例子：产出被成倍放大，但仍然需要开发者去管理 agent 干的活。Jevons 悖论依然成立。

featured.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
featured.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch shared his "holy s*" moments of the week—he thinks "WTFs/day" might be his favorite metric for AI progress. Concrete wins: Fable found a 15-30% memory efficiency improvement in Turbopack / Next.js nearly autonomously; three days ago Sol helped them find novel vulnerabilities in some of the most audited code in the world; and they shrank binaries by 10-20x. He says it's one thing to read benchmarks or online stories, and another to watch these machines pull engineering feats every day—and…
featured.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 分享了这周的「卧槽时刻」——他认为「每天卧槽次数」（WTFs/day）可能是衡量 AI 进展最好的指标。具体战果：Fable 几乎完全自主地在 Turbopack / Next.js 里找到了 15-30% 的内存效率提升；三天前 Sol 帮他们在全世界被审计得最彻底的代码里发现了新的漏洞；他们还把二进制文件体积缩小了 10-20 倍。他说读 benchmark 和看别人的故事是一回事，亲眼看着这些机器每天完成工程壮举是另一回事，而且这种感觉每周都在发生，还在加速。

featured.title: How Every's Team Used AI to Ship Its Biggest Launch Ever
featured.summaryEn: The real leverage isn't having AI write your code—it's keeping "framing the problem + reviewing the result" for yourself and handing the entire middle execution to an agent loop. Every's team used this to generate the largest subscription revenue increase in company history. The Every team (hosted by Dan Shipper, with Josh, Austin, Douglas and others) broke down their newly launched Builder Pack / All Access tier—a $625/year plan bundling exclusive perks (free credits and discounts) across ten AI tools including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Gemini, Notion, PostHog, Framer, Render, and Flora. It drove the biggest subscription revenue jump in company history. The most vivid case came from Austin: on launch night, Josh dropped an idea in Slack—email users who reached checkout but didn't convert with an urgency-backed push. Austin wanted to hit the gym, so he screenshotted the Slack thread in…
featured.insightZh: 真正的杠杆不是让 AI 帮你写代码，而是把「设定问题 + 评审结果」留给自己，中间的执行整段交给 agent 循环跑——Every 团队靠这套方法创造了公司史上最大的订阅收入增长。 Every 团队（Dan Shipper 主持，Josh、Austin、Douglas 等人参与）复盘了他们刚上线的 Builder Pack / All Access 新订阅层——一个 625 美元/年的计划，打包了 OpenAI、Anthropic、Cursor、Gemini、Notion、PostHog、Framer、Render、Flora 等十家 AI 工具的独家福利（免费额度和 credits）。它带来了公司史上最大的订阅收入增长。 最生动的案例来自 Austin：发布当天晚上，Josh 在 Slack 里丢了个想法——给那些走到结账页但没转化的用户发一封带紧迫感的邮件。Austin 想去健身房，于是他直接截了个 Slack 的图丢进 Codex（用 5.6 Sol / Medium），敲了个 `/LFG`（他们 compound engineering 插件里的「头脑风暴-规划-执行-评审」循环 harness），然后就去健身了。等他健身回来，Codex 已经自主完成了：切出 4 个基于行为的目标人群、给每类人起草了专属邮件、通过他们内部写作工具 Spiral 的 MCP 套上审核过的文风、翻查历史发送记录学习哪些措辞能拉高点击和打开率、抓了一张历史上转化好的社交图嵌进去、并排好了次日早晨的发送时间。他只花了十分钟做了点微调。第二天早上这几封邮件单独带来了 2.5 万美元以上的收入。 贯穿全场的一个心智模型是同事 Kieran 说的「AI 三明治」：你处在三明治的顶层和底层——你定义问题、框定想法（顶层），然后评审产出（底层），中间的执行交给 agent。创意总监 Douglas 补了个更妙的比喻：这套工具栈把工作从「演奏乐器」变成了「指挥乐团」——你不需要会演奏其它乐器，只要知道整首曲子该是什么声音，就能同时指挥好几个乐团。

items.title: Amjad Masad · Replit CEO
items.summaryEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad offered a sharp take on model routers: if you're incentivized to push certain models, your router is merely a facade. It's a direct shot at platforms marketing "smart model selection"—an incentive-bound router isn't actually picking the best option for the user. He was also showcasing Replit's mobile coding, claiming they invented mobile coding and are now taking it to the next level.
items.insightZh: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 对模型路由器（router）下了个挺尖锐的判断：如果你有动机去推某些特定模型，那你的路由器不过是个幌子。这是对当下一些平台「智能选模型」宣传的直接开炮——利益绑定的路由本质上不是在为用户选最优解。他同期还在秀 Replit 的移动端编程能力，说他们发明了移动编程、现在要把它推向下一个层级。

items.title: Madhu Guru · Meta AI 高级总监（前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人）
items.summaryEn: Meta AI Sr Director and former Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana lead Madhu Guru cleared up a common enterprise misconception: using a Chinese-trained LLM doesn't mean they get your data. His explanation is blunt—an LLM is basically a giant file full of numbers, and that's what encodes the intelligence. Some models let you download that file ("open weights") and run it on your own cloud environment, at which point the model trainer is out of the picture and your data stays wherever you're running it. A key clarificati…
items.insightZh: Meta AI 高级总监、前 Google Gemini/Veo/Nano Banana 负责人 Madhu Guru 澄清了一个企业界常见的误解：用中国训练的 LLM 不等于你的数据会被对方拿走。他的解释很直白——一个 LLM 本质上就是一个装满数字的巨大文件，智能就编码在这些数字里。有些模型允许你下载这个文件（「开放权重」）并在你自己的云环境里运行，这时候训练方就完全出局了，你的数据留在你运行它的地方。这对纠结「合规能不能用开源中国模型」的企业决策者是个关键澄清。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder（follow-builders 作者）
items.summaryEn: Builder Zara Zhang shared a practical insight on working with AI: sometimes she just describes the problem without specifying a solution or spec, and the model often surprises her with a better solution than she'd have thought of. She distills it as "Thick context, thin prompt." Paired with a companion note that communication and articulation is itself a hard skill. Together they argue that the leverage in the AI era isn't in crafting an elaborate prompt, but in providing rich context and stating the problem clear…
items.insightZh: Builder Zara Zhang 分享了一条很实用的 AI 协作心得：有时候她只描述问题、不指定解决方案或规格，模型反而经常给出比她自己能想到的更好的方案。她把这个总结成一句话——「厚上下文，薄提示」（Thick context, thin prompt）。配套的另一条观点是：沟通和表达本身就是一项很难的技能。这两条放一起，本质是在说 AI 时代的杠杆不在于把 prompt 写得多精细，而在于给足背景、把问题讲清楚。

items.title: Thariq · Anthropic Claude Code 团队
items.summaryEn: Anthropic Claude Code team member Thariq shared a hands-on note: he's sad it took him this long to actually type `/design`, but working on frontend with Claude Design and Claude Code is genuinely so good. A small tweet, but as first-hand feedback from a Claude Code engineer it's a useful signal on how usable Anthropic's frontend design toolchain actually is.
items.insightZh: Anthropic Claude Code 团队成员 Thariq 分享了一个上手体验：他后悔这么晚才真正开始用 `/design`，但用 Claude Design 加 Claude Code 做前端确实非常好用。这条本身流量不大，但作为来自 Claude Code 内部工程师的一手反馈，对判断 Anthropic 前端设计工具链的实际可用度有参考价值。

items.title: Claude (Anthropic) · 官方账号
items.summaryEn: Anthropic's official Claude account shipped two enterprise-relevant things this week. First, the Claude Security plugin for Claude Code is now in beta: scan your changes for vulnerabilities before you commit, or run a full scan across your codebase, all from your terminal on the Claude inference you already run (this one drew 12.8K+ likes). Second, the Anthropic Economic Index is now available as a connector—open it from the connectors menu, use it in any conversation, and the full datasets remain free to download.
items.insightZh: Anthropic 官方 Claude 账号本周发布了两个值得企业关注的东西。其一是 Claude Code 的 Claude Security 插件进入 beta：可以在提交前扫描你的改动找漏洞，或对整个代码库做全量扫描，全部在你自己已经在跑的 Claude 推理上、从终端里完成——这条互动量很高（1.2 万+ 赞）。其二是把 Anthropic 经济指数（Anthropic Economic Index）做成了 connector，在 connectors 菜单里就能打开，任何对话里都能用，完整数据集依旧免费下载。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: AI tutorials creator Peter Yang built a run of content this week around his `/no-ai-slop` skill. It picked up 1,000 GitHub stars in a day, and he quipped that "people are sick of slop." The fun twist: run it in reverse and it becomes very good at generating slop—he used it to reply to a friend complaining about too much LinkedIn slop with every AI cliché out there. The skill is free to grab.
items.insightZh: AI 教程创作者 Peter Yang 这周围绕他的 `/no-ai-slop`（反 AI 废话）skill 做了一系列内容。这个 skill 一天就拿了 1000 个 star，他调侃说「大家是真的受够了 slop（AI 生成的空洞垃圾内容）」。有意思的是他还展示了反向玩法：把 skill 倒过来用，它就能专门生成塞满每一句 AI 陈词滥调的废话——他用它给一个抱怨 LinkedIn 上废话太多的朋友回了一条极致 slop 的评论。skill 免费开放获取。

items.title: Nan Yu · Linear 产品负责人
items.summaryEn: Linear head of product Nan Yu posed a discussion-sparking question: when you hear or say "systems thinking," what's the exact definition in your head? It drew 82 replies. He also predicted it'll be the next big meme after "taste." A useful hook for product and team people to reflect on—many high-frequency abstract terms don't actually share a common definition across the people using them.
items.insightZh: Linear 产品负责人 Nan Yu 抛了个引发讨论的问题：当你听到或说出「系统性思维」（systems thinking）时，你脑子里那个确切的定义到底是什么？这条收了 82 条回复。他还顺带预言：这个词会成为继「taste（品味）」之后下一个大流行 meme。对做产品和团队的人来说，这是个值得自省的钩子——很多被高频使用的抽象词，大家心里的定义其实并不一致。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · South Park Commons 普通合伙人（前 Dropbox CTO）
items.summaryEn: South Park Commons GP and former Dropbox CTO Aditya Agarwal wrote on startup culture: everyone talks about strategy, but culture always eats strategy for breakfast. So where does startup culture come from? He gives three sources—the founder's personality and DNA, the early team's, and the early product's—all overlapping and reinforcing each other. Some is top-down, some emergent. He flags two failure modes: a founder too weak to institutionalize culture, which dampens emergence, and so much difference of opinion t…
items.insightZh: South Park Commons 普通合伙人、前 Dropbox CTO Aditya Agarwal 写了一段关于创业公司文化的思考：大家总在聊公司战略，但文化永远把战略当早餐吃掉。那创业公司的文化到底来自哪？他给了三个源头——创始人的个性与 DNA、早期团队的个性与 DNA、早期产品的个性与 DNA，三者互相重叠、互相强化。有些是自上而下的，有些是自发涌现的。他指出两种糟糕情况：一是创始人太弱、无法把文化制度化，导致自发涌现被人为压制；二是分歧太大，最后公司里长出一块块割裂的亚文化。
